headline: Your values are revealed by your actions, not your intentions
universal_truth: Knowing what you truly value is the foundation of an authentic life
fun_facts: Research shows a gap between what people say they value and how they actually spend their time and money

Psychologists have identified 10 universal values that appear across all cultures: power, achievement, hedonism, stimulation, self-direction, universalism, benevolence, tradition, conformity, and security
People who can articulate their core values make decisions 35% faster and report higher life satisfaction
discussion_questions: What do your calendar and bank statement reveal about what you actually value?
When have your stated values and actual behavior been misaligned?
Which of your values would you be unwilling to compromise?

hook.script: What do you care about most? It seems like an easy question—until you realize the answer isn't in what you say, but in what you do. Today we explore how to discover your true values and live in alignment with them.

cliff.script: Here's an uncomfortable truth: if you want to know someone's real values—including your own—don't ask. Watch. Look at how time and money are actually spent. What might this reveal?
cliff.prompt: Why are actions better than words for revealing values?

options.text: We lie to ourselves about what matters
options.response: Exactly. Not maliciously—but we believe what we want to be true. Actions cut through the self-deception.

options.text: Values are too abstract to express
options.response: There's some truth there. But the deeper issue is that our stated values often don't match our revealed ones.

fact1.title: Stated vs Revealed Values
fact1.script: Economists distinguish between stated preferences—what we say matters—and revealed preferences—what our behavior shows. The gap can be stunning. Someone might say family is their top value while working 80-hour weeks. Awareness of this gap is the first step to closing it.

fact2.title: The Values Hierarchy
fact2.script: Not all values are equal to you. The interesting question isn't what you value, but what you value more. When health and career conflict, which wins? When loyalty and honesty collide, which do you choose? Your hierarchy reveals your true priorities.

fact3.title: Values Alignment
fact3.script: Living in alignment means your daily actions reflect your deepest values. This doesn't require grand gestures—it's about small choices: how you spend a free hour, what you say yes and no to, how you treat people when no one's watching.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: You don't need perfect alignment—just honest awareness. Notice when your actions drift from your values. Gently course-correct. Over time, the gap shrinks and life feels more authentic.

outro.script: That's today's lesson on discovering what you truly care about. Tomorrow, we'll explore who you are when no one's looking. Until then, watch your choices—they're telling you something.

growTrack.title: Values Audit - The Reveal
growTrack.learning_objective: Compare stated values with revealed preferences through behavior analysis
growTrack.activity: Look at your last week's calendar and recent purchases. What do they suggest you truly value? Compare this to what you'd say if asked. Notice any gaps without judgment.
